title: Dynamic Programming Journey
description: State design, knapsack, grids, strings, stock states, interval splits, and memoized graph paths.

prerequisites: Basic graph traversal for the final milestone
journey.outcome: Define a sufficient state, derive transitions and base cases, then choose a dependency order before optimizing memory.

connections.climbing-stairs: Start by writing a recurrence for the last move. Memoization removes repeated calls; tabulation evaluates the same dependencies in increasing step order.
connections.min-cost-climbing-stairs: Keep the one-dimensional dependency graph, but replace counting with minimization. Define whether a state means reaching a step or paying for that step before writing the recurrence.
connections.frog-jump: Keep the same possible predecessors while making transition cost depend on both heights. The best previous total alone is insufficient without the cost of the chosen jump.
connections.maximum-subarray: Change the state to the best subarray ending at the current position. Either extend the previous answer or start again; the best ending here differs from the best seen anywhere.
connections.maximum-product-subarray: A negative multiplier reverses ordering, so the maximum-ending-here state needs a minimum-ending-here companion. This is an example of expanding state to preserve future-relevant information.
connections.house-robber: Return to take-or-skip choices, with taking an item forbidding its immediate predecessor. Distinguish the best answer for a prefix from a solution forced to include its last item.
connections.house-robber-ii: Reuse the linear robber solver twice. The circular constraint means the first and last houses cannot both participate, so solve the two possible endpoint exclusions.
connections.decode-ways: Switch from maximizing value to counting valid constructions. One- and two-character transitions look like stairs, but zeroes and the 1-to-26 range determine which edges exist.
connections.cses-1158: Book Shop is 0/1 knapsack: choose each book at most once under a price budget. Add a capacity dimension because two prefixes with different remaining budgets are not interchangeable.
connections.subset-sum-equals-to-target: Keep the one-use capacity recurrence but replace maximum pages with reachability. A boolean state records whether an exact target can be formed, not whether a budget can be underfilled.
connections.partition-equal-subset-sum: Reduce equal partition to the subset-sum solver. The total must be even, and finding one subset totaling half automatically determines the complementary subset.
connections.target-sum: Change boolean reachability into a count of signed assignments. Distinct choices involving zero still count separately; either track signed sums directly or derive a valid subset target.
connections.last-stone-weight-ii: Use subset partition to minimize the difference between two group totals. Unlike the heap-based stone-smashing exercise, always combining the largest stones is not the optimization argument here.
connections.unbounded-knapsack: Change exactly one modeling rule: an item may be reused. The take transition stays with the same item type, which reverses the safe iteration direction in a one-dimensional table.
connections.rod-cutting: Interpret reusable item weights as piece lengths and values as sale prices. The full rod length must be accounted for, so map array indices to physical lengths carefully.
connections.coin-change: Keep unlimited reuse and exact capacity, but minimize the number of selected items. Unreachable amounts need an impossible sentinel, not the zero used for valid empty selections.
connections.coin-change-ii: Replace minimum count with number of combinations. Coin-first iteration counts each multiset once; amount-first iteration can instead count different orders as different constructions.
connections.unique-paths: Move from a one-dimensional amount to a grid cell. The legal incoming directions define a two-dimensional counting recurrence and a straightforward row-by-row evaluation order.
connections.unique-paths-ii: Keep the same recurrence but delete blocked states. Obstacles also affect initialization, including the start, destination, first row, and first column.
connections.minimum-path-sum: Reuse the grid dependency order while switching counting to minimum accumulated cost. Each transition now adds the current cell value rather than combining path counts.
connections.triangle: The grid shape changes, but each cell still depends on a small set of neighbors. Bottom-up evaluation can eliminate awkward boundary branches at the triangle's edges.
connections.minimum-falling-path-sum: Allow three predecessor columns and any starting column. Use a fresh next row or preserve the previous row so updates do not consume partially overwritten states.
connections.ninjas-training: Replace a spatial column with the activity selected today. The previous activity is the state needed to enforce the no-repeat transition constraint across days.
connections.longest-increasing-subsequence: A transition may come from any earlier smaller value, not just neighboring indices. Begin with quadratic ending-at-index DP before considering the faster tails-array formulation.
connections.longest-common-subsequence: Use one prefix position per sequence. A character match extends both prefixes; otherwise dropping one end yields overlapping subproblems rather than a single greedy choice.
connections.longest-palindromic-subsequence: Apply subsequence reasoning to a palindrome. Matching interval endpoints can contribute together; unlike a substring problem, unmatched characters may be skipped.
connections.distinct-subsequences: Keep two prefix coordinates, but count the ways the source can form the target. Matching characters allow both using and skipping that source occurrence.
connections.word-break: Choose the last dictionary word of a prefix. The state is whether its preceding prefix is constructible, connecting string segmentation to the take-a-piece recurrences from coin problems.
connections.longest-palindromic-substring: Now contiguity is mandatory. An interval is palindromic only if its endpoints match and its interior is palindromic; center expansion is a useful alternative to the table.
connections.palindromic-substrings: Reuse palindrome recognition but count every valid interval instead of retaining only the longest one. Equal spellings at different positions are separate substrings here.
connections.edit-distance: Use two prefixes again, with insertion, deletion, and replacement edges carrying costs. Empty-prefix base cases represent real sequences of edits, not impossible states.
connections.interleaving-string: Track how much of each source has been consumed. Their prefix lengths determine the position in the target, so a third coordinate would store redundant information.
connections.wildcard-matching: Add pattern states to prefix matching. A star can consume nothing or one more input character, while a question mark consumes exactly one; initialize empty-input cases carefully.
connections.regular-expression-matching: Interview stretch: the star now repeats the preceding atom rather than matching arbitrary text by itself. Re-derive its transitions instead of copying the wildcard recurrence.
connections.best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii: Model trading with two states: holding a share or holding cash. Multiple transactions are allowed, but buying and selling must respect what the previous state actually owns.
connections.best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-coo: Expand the stock state because cash obtained by selling today cannot buy tomorrow. Track holding, just-sold, and resting states or encode the required lookback explicitly.
connections.best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-with-tra: Return to two trading states and add a transaction cost exactly once. Comparing this with cooldown separates a cost change from a change in legal transitions.
connections.matrix-chain-multiplication: Switch from choosing a next move to choosing the final split of an interval. Smaller intervals must be solved first, and matrix dimensions determine the cost of combining two results.
connections.burst-balloons: Reuse interval splitting, but choose which balloon is removed last. Its outside neighbors then remain fixed, making the left and right subintervals independent.
connections.palindrome-partitioning-ii: Combine palindrome recognition with prefix optimization. Precompute which intervals are palindromes, then minimize the cuts before the final palindromic piece.
connections.longest-increasing-path-in-a-matrix: Finish with memoization on an implicit DAG. Strictly increasing values prevent cycles, so the best path from a cell can be cached and reused by every predecessor.

topics.name: Recurrences and state design
topics.description: Translate choices into states, base cases, memoization, and tabulation before compressing memory.

topics.name: 0/1 choices and subset targets
topics.description: Distinguish maximizing value, exact reachability, counting choices, and minimizing a partition difference.

topics.name: Unbounded choices and coin patterns
topics.description: Allow reuse deliberately and make loop order match combinations rather than permutations.

topics.name: Grids and constrained transitions
topics.description: Change dimensions, obstacles, costs, and legal predecessors without losing the state invariant.

topics.name: Subsequence families
topics.description: Preserve order while allowing gaps, then change optimization into counting.

topics.name: String prefixes, intervals, and matching
topics.description: Separate segmentation, contiguous palindromes, edit operations, and pattern semantics.

topics.name: Stock state machines
topics.description: Track ownership and legal transactions, then distinguish cooldown constraints from fees.

topics.name: Interval splits and partition costs
topics.description: Choose a final split or final action so independently solved subproblems can be combined.

topics.name: Memoization on a DAG
topics.description: Recognize an acyclic dependency graph even when it is represented as a matrix.
